candidates.author: Cole Medin
candidates.organization: Cole Medin (YouTube); tool shown is Cloudflare's security-audit skill
candidates.length: UNVERIFIED; chapter list runs past 11:55 (feed description truncated there), so roughly 12-14 min
candidates.sponsored: yes: integrated sponsor read for Eney by MacPaw at 5:07-6:28; description also promotes his own Dynamous Black Friday sale / AI Software Factory bootcamp (Dec 2)
candidates.worth_watching: 6:28-11:55 (Cloudflare skill: install 7:38, run on his own project 8:08, hunters and verifiers 8:52, findings 10:15, proving and fixing the bug 10:32). Skip 5:07-6:28 (sponsor). 2:31-5:07 is useful framing: how attackers find vulns, a 'Java4Shell' bug found in an hour (UNVERIFIED name/claim), 'the five questions attackers ask'.
candidates.what_changed: A practitioner walkthrough of running Cloudflare's open-source security-audit coding-agent skill against your own repo before attackers' agents do, then proving and fixing what it finds.
candidates.mechanism: Linked repo github.com/cloudflare/security-audit-skill (MIT; README read via raw.githubusercontent.com): six-phase audit run by isolated agents: (1) Reconnaissance writes architecture.md and coverage-ledger.json (trust boundaries, input surfaces, deterministic coverage); (2) coverage-led hunting with isolated hunters assigned from ledger units plus 'coverage critics' to find gaps; (3) every unique candidate goes to a fresh verifier that tries to disprove it; (4) structured output to findings.json validated against report-schema.json with three verdicts: confirmed (complete source trace + bounded observed result), needs_validation (exact unresolved fact, no severity), rejected; (5) independent record verification by fresh agents; (6) target-neutral reports REPORT.md / FINDINGS-DETAIL.md / NEEDS-VALIDATION.md. Zero-dependency Node validators validate-coverage-ledger.cjs and validate-findings.cjs run after each ledger update and in Phases 4-5. Per-class hunting files include AI-AND-LLM.md (prompt injection, agent/tool, output handling), SUPPLY-CHAIN-AND-RELEASE.md, CLOUD-AND-DEPLOYMENT.md, DATA-ISOLATION-AND-LIFECYCLE.md, RESOURCE-EXHAUSTION (incl. operator spend), etc. Install: npx skills add https://github.com/cloudflare/security-audit-skill --skill security-audit [--global]. Trigger phrases like 'security audit this codebase'. Default output dir ~/security-audit-skill/<repo-name>/run-<N>; writes inside the target repo only if you pick a VCS-ignored dir. Requires an OS-enforced sandbox (no external network, sanitized allowlisted env, resource limits, writes only to scratch paths) to execute target code; without it leads stay needs_validation. Runs are additive: prior ledgers/findings target gaps and revalidate changed source. Design principles: only confirm established boundary failures; the checking agent is never the finding agent; severity = likelihood x impact; defense-in-depth gaps are hardening notes not vulns; 'a single run found roughly half of the vulnerabilities that repeated runs found in total'.
candidates.evidence_quality: Video content beyond chapter titles UNVERIFIED (YouTube page not readable by fetch; only RSS description). Skill details confirmed from the repo README. Background: Cloudflare blog 'Build your own vulnerability harness' (2026-06-18, https://blog.cloudflare.com/build-your-own-vulnerability-harness) says the skill was ~450 lines and seeded their fleet-wide harness; three walls they hit: context exhaustion (fixed by externalizing state, LLM as stateless compute), persistence across crashes, cross-repo reasoning; advice: minimal harness = Recon, Hunt, Validate stages in a database plus a separate Validator that can't file its own findings; vary models between discovery and validation.
candidates.independent_confirmation: Repo README and Cloudflare June blog are primary sources; Cole's results on his own project are single-author demo (UNVERIFIED).
candidates.relevance: High: actionable this week; directly continues Edition 5's agent-security thread with a defender-side, verifier-separated audit loop.
candidates.overlap_with_prior: Prior URLs include blog.cloudflare.com/adapting-to-ai-penetration-testing-orchestrators (a different Cloudflare post). The security-audit-skill repo and this video are not in prior URLs. Cole's Nov 23 video 'Hackers Are Coming for Your AI Coding Agent' is outside window.
candidates.summary: Cole Medin's Nov 26 video argues attackers now use AI agents to find and exploit bugs fast, so builders should run the same approach on their own code first. He installs Cloudflare's free, MIT-licensed security-audit skill and runs it against one of his own projects, showing the hunter/verifier split in action and then proving and fixing a real finding. The skill (the seed of Cloudflare's fleet-wide vulnerability harness) runs a six-phase audit: recon to architecture.md + coverage-ledger.json, isolated coverage-led hunters with coverage critics, a fresh adversarial verifier per candidate, schema-validated findings.json with confirmed / needs_validation / rejected verdicts, independent re-verification by fresh agents, and generated reports. Two zero-dependency Node validators mechanically check the ledger and findings. It needs parallel sub-agents and an OS-enforced, network-disabled sandbox to execute target code; otherwise leads stay needs_validation. Cloudflare says one run finds about half of what repeated runs find, and runs are additive. Sponsored (Eney by MacPaw at 5:07); watch 6:28 to the end.

candidates.title: Copilot code review billing will default to the organization
candidates.author: GitHub
candidates.what_changed: For Copilot Business/Enterprise orgs that never chose a billing option for Copilot code review by licensed members, reviews will be billed to the organization owning the repo starting December 30, 2026, instead of to the member's Copilot entitlement.
candidates.mechanism: Today an unset setting means reviews by members with a paid Copilot license consume the member's entitlement. From Dec 30, unset = Organization billing (requires AI Credits paid usage; 'can increase your organization's spending'). Accounts without AI Credits paid usage enabled, with a billing lock, or with no billable customer get set to Member instead. Saved Member/Organization choices persist. Until then, unset settings show 'Default (Member)' with a notice. To keep current behavior: select Member in enterprise or org Copilot policy settings (enterprise owner if enterprise-managed). Separate setting for members without a Copilot license is unchanged.
candidates.relevance: Medium: concrete AI-cost action item with a deadline.
candidates.overlap_with_prior: Edition 5 briefed the Nov 23 usage-report user_id column; this is a separate billing change.
candidates.summary: GitHub will flip the default billing for Copilot code review: if an org/enterprise on Copilot Business or Enterprise hasn't chosen, reviews by licensed members will bill to the repo-owning organization (AI Credits paid usage) from Dec 30, 2026 rather than to the member's entitlement. Orgs without paid AI Credits, with a billing lock, or no billable customer stay on Member. To avoid surprise spend, set Member explicitly in Copilot policy settings before Dec 30.
